title: Two white cloths
hookLine: men wear two unstitched white cloths; women wear modest ordinary clothes
last: AT THE MIQAT, A TRAVELER BECOMES A PILGRIM.

lines: THE CLOTHES FROM HOME COME OFF.
NOBODY CAN TELL WHO IS WHO.
cards: Two pieces of white cloth. No seams, no buttons, no collar, no label. One wraps the waist, the other goes over the shoulders.
That's the whole outfit. A pilgrim reaches yesterday's boundary, takes off the clothes that said who he was at home, the suit or the uniform or the team jersey, and puts these on.
The man next to him does the same, and the man next to him. Within an hour, you can't tell the surgeon from the taxi driver. Today, the word for what has just happened to them.

teach.h: A STATE, NOT JUST A CLOTH.
teach.b: First, the word. Ihram isn't really the name of the cloth. It's a state the pilgrim enters, at the boundary, with an intention.
The two cloths are how that state looks from outside, and people call them the ihram too. Second, how the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ described it. Someone asked him what a person in ihram should wear.
The report is in Sahih al-Bukhari, and his answer is a surprise: he didn't describe the outfit. He listed what to leave off. No shirts, no turbans, no trousers, no hooded cloaks, no leather socks.
The clothes are defined by what's missing. Whatever is cut and sewn to the shape of a body, with its fashion and its rank, stays home. Third, the women.
A woman in ihram doesn't wrap herself in two white cloths.
She wears her own ordinary, modest clothes, and another report in Bukhari says she doesn't wear a face veil or gloves in that state. So the rule isn't one uniform for everybody.
It's simplicity for everybody, in the shape that fits. Fourth, what it does.
Put a crowd from everywhere into the same plain dress, and the usual signals go quiet. Nobody's watch is on show. Nobody's accent shows in the cut of a coat.
Some pilgrims say the two white cloths remind them of a shroud, plain cloth like the cloth Muslims are buried in, and that thought travels with them the whole journey.
Whatever the cloth means to a given pilgrim, the effect is the same. For a few days, the person inside it is just a person, standing among people, dressed alike.

how: Men entering ihram for Hajj or Umrah put on two unstitched white cloths, one around the waist and one over the shoulders; women wear their own modest clothes. Pilgrims make their intention at the miqat and stay in ihram until the rites release them.

practice: Take off one thing you wear partly so people will notice it, a logo, a watch, a piece of jewelry, and set it aside. Sit for a moment and notice whether you feel any lighter, or any barer.
If you pray, hold the picture of the pilgrims in their plain cloth and say a verse you know; if not, stay with the breath, being nobody in particular.
